title: Indian Contract Act, 1872 — Section 189 (Agent’s authority in an emergency)

content.overview: Section 189 provides that an agent has authority, in an emergency, to do all such acts for the purpose of protecting his principal from loss as would be done by a person of ordinary prudence, in his own case, under similar circumstances.
content.glance: In an emergency, an agent has authority to do all such acts for the purpose of protecting the principal from loss as a person of ordinary prudence would do in his own case under similar circumstances.
content.study: An agent has authority, in an emergency, to do all such acts for the purpose of protecting his principal from loss as would be done by a person of ordinary prudence, in his own case, under similar circumstances. Current-law framing: emergency authority measured by the standard of ordinary prudence for protecting the principal from loss.

sections.heading: Core rule
sections.body: An agent has authority, in an emergency, to do all such acts for the purpose of protecting his principal from loss as would be done by a person of ordinary prudence, in his own case, under similar circumstances.

examples.title: Emergency protection
examples.body: In an emergency the agent may take steps a person of ordinary prudence would take to protect the principal from loss, under Section 189.
